days.note: Wed - Brent $79.45 (TradingEconomics Jun 17, +0.6% minor bounce; -19% from D93 $98.57 peak). WTI $75.47; TTF €41.12 (-1.6%). At three-month lows. 2 days to MOU signing. Iran differing MOU versions + nuclear sequencing unresolved; deputy FM frozen-funds condition. Deal fragile but signing track intact. Tail 15%.

Thu - MOU digitally pre-signed at G7 Versailles (Jun 18, Haaretz). Formal ceremony at Burgenstock tomorrow. Brent $79.34 (TradingEconomics, -0.27%); WTI $76.43 (-0.47%); TTF €41.33 (-1.39%). Markets pricing deal confirmation. Tail 12%.

Fri - MOU formally signed Burgenstock, Switzerland — formal ceremony complete. Phase 2 nuclear talks begin immediately. US markets closed Juneteenth; Brent $79.34 carried (Jun 18 close). Escalation lowered to 2 (Elevated). Tail 10%.

Fri - First trading day after Juneteenth. Phase 2 nuclear talks in Switzerland abruptly postponed (CNBC). Iran disputes MOU text elements. Brent ~$79.80 est. (small rise on postponement uncertainty). Tail 11% (small reversal on postponement news).
Sat - Market closed; scenarios carried from D110.
Sun - US-Iran Phase 2 nuclear talks kick off in Switzerland (Al Jazeera). Vance leads US delegation. Oil futures open; Brent ~$79.25 (Fortune 8:45am ET). Roadmap talks positive signal. Tail 10%.

Mon - Vance-Iran first round concludes: 'roadmap toward final deal within 60 days' agreed (Al Jazeera/CNBC/NPR). IAEA inspectors 'invited' per Vance; Iran FM disputes. Lebanon deconfliction mechanism agreed. Brent ~$78.00 est. (-1.6%). Technical talks continue in Switzerland. Tail 10%.

Tue - Brent crashes -5.3% to $73.87 (Barchart implied) as tankers transit Hormuz; Goldman Sachs cuts Q4 Brent to $80 from $90 (Investing.com) — expects GCC exports normalised by end-Jul. WTI briefly below $70 (CNBC). Brent erasing wartime gains (Bloomberg). Tail 9%.

Wed - Brent $75.04 (TradingEconomics confirmed, +1.76% from $73.87 Jun 24 close). WTI ~$69.95 est. (below $70 Jun 25, CNBC). Partial rebound after steep sell-off. Gold $4,040.30 (TradingEconomics confirmed, +1.02%). Mine-clearing Day 6 of 30-day mandate. Technical talks continue. Tail 9%.

Thu - Brent ~$75.04 carried (Jun 25 confirmed; Jun 26 not yet confirmed). Roadmap agreed Jun 22-23; IAEA access disputed but Grossi says inspections 'will take place.' Mine-clearing Day 7 of 30-day mandate. Goldman Q4 $80 Brent. iTraxx ~128bp est. EM FX strengthening. Tail 8%.

Tue - Brent $73.68 (+0.7% from Mon). Guardian reveals Iran rejected Oman/UN route, attacked Singaporean tanker Jun 25, IMO abandoned plan. Central route mined; Iran insists sole control. France/UK naval taskforce ready. Markets pricing normalisation but reopening deeply contested. Tail raised 15%.

Wed - Brent $76.05 (+6.3%). Guardian reports US strikes around Hormuz after Iran hit three commercial vessels including Qatari LNG tanker Al Rekayyat. Axios reports oil waivers revoked Jul 7. MOU credibility damaged; tail 20%.
Thu - Brent $76.03 (+5.6%). Axios reports second-day US strikes and a regional mediation push; AP reports Iranian retaliation against US infrastructure in three Gulf states. Tail 22%.

Sun - Weekend escalation: Iran declared Hormuz closed and struck container ship GFS Galaxy; US hit 140 targets in third strike wave; Iran retaliated across Jordan, Qatar, Oman, Kuwait. Brent $76.01 (Friday close — not yet reflecting escalation). Tail 55%.

Tue - Trump orders Hormuz blockade, 20% cargo tribute; US strikes Iran third consecutive night; IRGC hits Duqm, Oman; Iran extends strikes to Qatar, UAE for first time in months. Brent $84.70 (+8.56%). Tail 65%.

Fri - US strikes Iran 6th consecutive day; CENTCOM hits Greater Tunb Island; US Navy interdicts tanker skirting blockade; Iran warns of regional infrastructure strikes; Brent $85.42 (+2.55%). Tail 65%.

Sat - US strikes Iran 7th consecutive night; expands to infrastructure (bridges, port tower, power plants); Iran hits Kuwait desalination plant, threatens full-scale offensive operations; Hormuz traffic at 3-week low (Kpler: 8 transits); Brent $88.09 (+5.75%). Tail 70%.
Mon - US pauses Iran strikes for 3rd day after 13 consecutive nights; Omani Hormuz talks in Tehran; tanker hits mine in strait; Brent $91.91 (-5% from Jul 24 $96.78); tail 45%.

Tue - US pause extends to 4th day after 13 consecutive nights; Iran confirms Omani Hormuz talks but denies direct US negotiations; Saudi intercepts Iraq-launched drones; Brent $86.72, down 7.81%; TTF eases to 58.70; tail 40%.
Wed - US pause extends to 5th day; Iran confirms Omani Hormuz talks ongoing; Saudi intercepts Iraq-launched drones; Brent 6.81, down 13.78%; TTF 56.50 EUR/MWh, down 8.72%; tail 40%.

Thu - Pause breaks after 5 days; Iran missile attack on US Jordan base intercepted; US/Saudi retaliate in Iraq, first Saudi offensive strikes of war; Trump vows 'beating'; Brent $89.46, up from $86.81 close; tail 60%.
Fri - US strikes dozens of IRGC targets; Iran launches another barrage at Jordan and Kuwait; Hormuz weekly traffic halves; Brent $88.00; tail 70%.
Sat - Iran attacks Kuwait; a tanker is struck near Hormuz; US threatens more strikes; Gulf mediators press for reopening; Brent $90.12; tail 70%.
Mon - Trump cancels planned Iran strikes, calls deal imminent; Oman-Iran Hormuz talks reach final stage; Brent -4.9% to $83.61; tail cut to 45%.
Tue - Iran denies full Hormuz deal, calls talks 'Oman-only' on a temporary corridor; tanker struck off Oman; Brent +0.8% to $84.28; tail raised to 47%.
Wed - Bessent says US-Iran Hormuz deal could come 'today or tomorrow'; Qatar floats de-escalation resolution; Brent -5.8% to $78.88 Tue then ~flat at $79.18; level cut to 4; tail 30%.
